findings.sentence: A total of five cis-eQTLs showing an association with epilepsy in the expected direction (p < 0.05) were considered validated instruments and carried forward to the primary and exploratory analyses.

findings.sentence: In sequence-resolved analyses (Table S3), both transition patterns in SHARE showed comparable negative point estimates relative to 00-for visit-2 initiation (01 vs 00), β = -0.0051 SD/year in global cognition and -0.0032 SD/year in memory; for visit-2 discontinuation (10 vs 00), β = -0.0038 and -0.0055 SD/year, respectively-whereas consistent two-visit reporting (11 vs 00) remained near zero (+0.0016 and +0.0015 SD/year), with no significant difference between patterns 01 and 10 (all P ≥ 0.237).
None of the 12 primary count contrasts survived familywise correction (all Holm P ≥ 0.410).
In SHARE, all count contrasts were close to zero (global cognition: -0.0020, -0.0065 and +0.0012 SD/year; memory: -0.0008, -0.0054 and -0.0006 SD/year; all P ≥ 0.23; all Holm P = 1.000).

In sensitivity analyses (Table S12), inverse-probability weights for completing all three exposure waves had mean predicted probabilities of 0.80 in HRS and 0.46 in SHARE, with Kish effective sample sizes of 12,316 and 24,018 and maximum weights of 1.39 and 1.52; weighted slope estimates were virtually unchanged (HRS global cognition 1 vs 0 visits: β = -0.0134 SD/year, 95% CI -0.0258 to -0.0011, P = 0.033; HRS memory 3 vs 0 visits: β = -0.0194 SD/year, 95% CI -0.0385 to -0.0003, P = 0.046; all SHARE contrasts P ≥ 0.266).

Restricting to face-to-face (CAPI) interviews left all SHARE estimates null (n = 12,079; all P ≥ 0.489); in the much smaller HRS face-to-face-only subset (n = 790 across all exposure groups), memory contrasts were null (all P ≥ 0.695) and global-cognition models were not estimated because exposed subgroup cells fell below the prespecified minimum threshold (n < 100) required for mixed-effects convergence.

Similarly, Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) showed a 10.13% higher value in the yoga group (84.96 ± 9.85) compared to the sedentary population (76.84 ± 19.75), with stronger statistical significance (p ≤ 0.01).

The FEV₁/FVC ratio, an important indicator of airway function and obstruction, was also significantly higher among yoga practitioners (76.21 ± 7.38) than non-yoga individuals (72.09 ± 14.25), indicating better airway patency and ventilatory efficiency (p ≤ 0.01).

findings.sentence: We found a significant positive correlation between the PPVT-5 standard score and the Penn-CNB Global Accuracy score (R=0.669, p<2.2E-16; Figure 2E).

Subjects with 3q29del had a 10-20% slower response speed compared to controls on four of the five Penn-CNB domains (Executive, Episodic memory, Social cognition, and Sensorimotor; all p<0.005), with a suggestive reduction in response speed on the Complex cognition domain (6% difference; p=0.078; Figure 3C, Table S4).
Response speed on the Continuous performance and Matrix reasoning tasks was relatively well-preserved in 3q29del participants compared to controls (p>0.300).
Individuals with 3q29dup had a 10-15% slower response speed compared to controls on two of the five domains (Social cognition and Sensorimotor; all p<0.05; Figure 3C, Table S4).
There were no differences in response speed between 3q29dup subjects and controls for the Executive, Episodic memory, or Complex cognition domains (all p>0.250; Figure 3C, Table S4).

Regarding speed, subjects with 3q29del were significantly slower than subjects with 3q29dup on three of the five speed domains (Executive, Episodic memory, and Social cognition), with the most substantial difference in Episodic memory (3q29del mean=80.07±30.50, 3q29dup mean=92.98±23.74, p=0.026), while response speed on the Complex cognition and Sensorimotor domains was not significantly different between 3q29del and 3q29dup (all p>0.300, Figure 3C, Table S4).
Subjects with 3q29del scored an average of 21.7 points, or 1.5 standard deviations, lower than their unaffected relatives (3q29del mean=84.11±14.29, 3q29del relative mean=105.76±8.58, p<2.2E-16).

There were no differences in Penn-CNB Global Accuracy between controls and any unaffected relative sample (all p>0.350; Figure S3B), suggesting that unaffected relatives of 3q29del and 3q29dup probands have similar cognitive ability compared to controls, but slowed neurocognitive processing speed.

On average, subjects with 3q29del scored more than one standard deviation below their unaffected relatives on Global Accuracy (average shift=-18.87±12.31, p<2.2E-16), with shift values ranging from -56.87 to 11.98 (Figure 4C).
Sex and age of the proband did not have an impact on the degree of shift in cognition (all p>0.450).

Shift values were not different between the original and first-degree relative-only analyses (all p>0.750, Table S5), indicating that the inclusion of non-first-degree relatives did not influence the analysis.

findings.sentence: Pressure-related variables were most frequently associated with ICU admissions (p ≤ 0.05).

For predictors exhibiting significant heterogeneity (adjusted p < 0.05), pairwise z-tests were performed, comparing sexes within age groups and age groups within sexes.
Across all models, the three pressure-related variables (SLP, SLPD, wind day) showed most frequently statistically significant associations (p ≤ 0.05) with ICU admissions.
SLP was significantly associated with NSTEMI admissions (p ≤ 0.05) in all subgroup models except for female <60 years.
No air pollutant was significantly associated with NSTEMI admissions (p ≤ 0.05), and the effect estimates were close to zero (Figure 3, Supplementary, Figure S13).
